headline: Civilization V fleets now need a port
lede: The shelf's weakest title learned naval supply: hulls more than six sea hexes from a friendly port wear 10 HP every turn, cannot heal afloat, and sink with their hold. Coastal cities and alliances are now the fleet's reach.

notes.text: NAVY REBALANCED — supply lines: a hull is supplied within 6 sea steps of an own/vassal/allied-city-state coastal port; far hulls wear, starve of heals, and attrition alone can drown a convoy with both squads aboard. Deep water is no longer a free highway; taking the coast is the fleet's lifeline.

35 new gates in civcheck §39 (594 total green): port law, horizon sharp at exactly 6 steps, exact wear, sink-and-drown, land-exempt, determinism — and a mutant (neuter the wear) dies on 7 live checks.

Honest framing (#237): Civ V has no attrition at sea — its real law is heals-on-friendly-territory-only with borders reaching the water. This ships the honest extension as arcade rules, and the README says so out loud.
Tells on the board: amber warning ring on unsupplied hulls, HUD chip naming the danger, and a log line when the crew reports out of supply.

look.text: Strand a trireme mid-channel and watch the ring light up
